boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Bonaventure rituals, recurring practices and campus symbols rooted in the university’s Franciscan community.

cards.title: Begin with Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Welcome Weekend tradition
cards.notes: Attend if invited during Welcome Weekend; the ceremony marks new students’ entry into the Bonaventure community with a candlelit walk and pledge.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit welcome rite for incoming students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture reported that the Candlelight Ceremony had been a St. Bonaventure tradition for more than 15 years and included a candlelit pathway and the university pledge.
cards.source_title: Staff and students ‘reflect’ on school tradition
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Welcome Weekend; participation details vary by year.

cards.title: Close the Journey by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Senior-year counterpart to Welcome Weekend
cards.notes: Look for senior-year commencement programming; this reflective ceremony mirrors the welcome ritual rather than repeating the first-year event.
cards.short_summary: A bookend ceremony connecting arrival and graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture reported that St. Bonaventure holds a specialized Candlelight Ceremony for seniors, so students begin and end their university journeys with parallel commemorations.
cards.source_title: Staff and students ‘reflect’ on school tradition
cards.access_notes: Timing and participation are determined through senior-year university programming.

cards.title: Watch for the First-Snow Mass
cards.subtitle: The Grotto, after the season’s first snowfall
cards.notes: If it is announced, dress for winter and follow campus-ministry guidance; the revived gathering is held outdoors at the Grotto after first snow.
cards.short_summary: A midnight Grotto Mass tied to the first snowfall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture documented Snow Mass as an old Bonaventure tradition begun in 1999, later revived in 2025, with students gathering at the Grotto after the first snowfall.
cards.source_title: First Snowfall, Lasting Tradition: Snow Mass at St. Bonaventure
cards.access_notes: Occurrence depends on snowfall and campus-ministry announcements; outdoor winter conditions apply.

cards.title: Mark the Transitus
cards.subtitle: Annual Franciscan remembrance
cards.notes: Check Campus Ministry’s fall schedule and attend respectfully; the service reflects on St. Francis’ passing and the university’s Franciscan roots.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus observance of St. Francis’ death.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture described the Transitus as a long-standing yearly Bonaventure tradition celebrating St. Francis’ passing from life to death.
cards.access_notes: Consult Campus Ministry for the current date, location and service format.

cards.title: Gather at the Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Marchiori Pavilion
cards.notes: Watch university event notices near the holiday season; the president-established gathering takes place at Marchiori Pavilion.
cards.short_summary: A newer annual holiday gathering at Marchiori Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Bonaventure states that President Jeff Gingerich established the annual Christmas tree lighting at Marchiori Pavilion as a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: SBU trustees OK contract extension for President Gingerich
cards.access_notes: Annual scheduling and event details are announced by the university.

cards.title: Carry the BonaResponds Legacy
cards.subtitle: Student disaster-relief and local-service practice
cards.notes: Join an announced service project or relief response through BonaResponds; its work grew from students’ 2006 Hurricane Katrina service trip.
cards.short_summary: Service work that became a defining Bonaventure practice.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Bonaventure says BonaResponds was born when students traveled to help after Hurricane Katrina in 2006 and has since aided thousands of people in need.
cards.access_notes: Volunteer opportunities and response deployments vary; use the organization’s current announcements.

cards.title: Continue the Warming House Service
cards.subtitle: Olean-area student-run meal service
cards.notes: Volunteer through the Franciscan Center for Social Concern when openings are posted; students have sustained this local service effort since 1974.
cards.short_summary: A long-running student service tradition in the Olean area.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Bonaventure states that students started the drop-in center now called The Warming House in 1974 and that it remains one of the nation’s oldest student-run soup kitchens.
cards.access_notes: Volunteer participation is organized through current service-program channels.

cards.title: Become a Bona Buddy
cards.subtitle: Student mentoring with local children
cards.notes: Ask the service office about current enrollment and screening; Bona Buddies connects students with local children for supportive mentorship.
cards.short_summary: A Bonaventure mentoring practice with local children.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Bonaventure identifies Bona Buddies as students serving as big brothers and sisters to local children needing a guiding influence.
cards.access_notes: Participation may require current program registration and training.

cards.title: Join the Wolf Pack at Reilly
cards.subtitle: Men’s basketball student section
cards.notes: Use current student-ticket and arena guidance for home games; the Wolf Pack is the named student section supporting Bonnies men’s basketball.
cards.short_summary: The named student section that gathers at Bonnies home games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture identifies the Wolf Pack as the nickname for St. Bonaventure’s student section at men’s basketball home games.
cards.access_notes: Home-game entry and student-section procedures are set by Athletics for each season.

cards.title: Listen for the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Doyle Hall and University Chapel bell tower
cards.notes: Pause by Doyle Hall to view the three-column tower and hear its bells; campus sources describe it as a longstanding Bonaventure emblem.
cards.short_summary: A bell tower whose design carries Bonaventure symbolism.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bona Venture reported that Our Lady’s Campanile has been a Bonaventure emblem since its 1961 dedication and is a recognizable mark of campus tradition and culture.
cards.source_title: Every time a bell rings, a Bonnie gets its wings
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; view from campus pathways and respect any building-access restrictions.
